record_verbatim.objective: Confirm that the master software completes no externally reachable network session with a peer that has not authenticated, and that after authentication the session's application payload is neither recoverable in plaintext by an observer on the segment nor modifiable by one. Also confirm that each refusal is diagnosable, because a silent refusal cannot be distinguished from an outage during field analysis.

oracle_detail.residual_risk: A source-grounded oracle still rests on the implementation using the mechanism the requirement names. If the implementation used a different mechanism, this oracle would be measuring the wrong thing.
oracle_detail.what_it_still_does_not_prove: It does not prove the item uses such a mode, that the key is stored well, that the mode is non-negotiable, or that the authentication cannot be bypassed by a different path. It also cannot prove the 'confidentiality of session data' acceptance criterion as a field observation, only as an inspection against the protocol's own guarantees.
oracle_detail.what_the_oracle_is_not: It is not a measured reference: no capture exists and nothing was replayed. It is not an analytical model: no model of the key exchange is computed here. It is not a synthetic assumption: the property asserted is a property of a primitive, not an assumption about this programme.
oracle_detail.why_this_oracle: The oracle is the cryptography's own definition, read from the requirement rather than from the implementation. 'A peer that cannot produce the key cannot produce a session it can decrypt' is a property of authenticated encryption, and it is checkable against the implementation by inspection: if the item uses an authenticated mode with a key the peer must possess, an observer without the key recovers nothing, and a modified frame fails authentication by definition of the mode. The expected outcomes are therefore not copied from what the item produced; they are what the chosen mode permits.

preconditions: The service is externally reachable in the configuration under test, which is the hypothetical project's planned commissioning service, not the one that exists in the pinned source.
The item is otherwise in a nominal mode with no active fault.
A capture point exists on the segment.
record_verbatim.regression_selection: Re-run on every change to the service's authentication path, to the cryptographic library, to the key-derivation or storage, and to the session timeout. Also re-run once per release because the acceptance criteria are zero-tolerance and a single regression fails the whole measure.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
